All abilities that allow any minion to play a card that requires something
which the minion lacks as "as if this minion has/is that required something
(but only for the purposes of playing the card)".

> If it allows her to meet the requirement of the card and have the
> required attribute for card text as played (but not thereafter) ...

This one is correct. (Snip other two)

> you could play and use ventrue headquarters
> you could play and be considered a ventrue during ventrue justicar

Note that after being named Ventrue Justicar, the title would
immeditely fall inert until such time as she changes clan and
sect to become a Camarilla Ventrue.

> you could not play and use the art of pain

She could use it. It is only "this vampire" for the in-play effect.

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew

> Wha?? Art of Pain says "Put this card on a ready Toreador Antitribu".
> She isn't one. I assumed her ability just allowed her to get around
> requirements for putting the card into play from your hand, e.g. the
> requirement on Ventrue Headquarters, not for being a vampire of type X
> when playing a card that says "put this card on a X".

Exactly. She gets around the requirements for putting the card into play.
In order to put the Art of Pain into play, it has to believe that she is
Toreador Antitribu. So you can put it on her.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
"Brendan Hunt" <Frea...@yahoo.com> wrote in message news:8e30270.05031...@posting.google.com...
[Re: Mata Hari and Art of Pain]

> So you would say that she can play the card, as if she were of the
> required clan, but the card cannot be played on herself because the
> card text (and not the requirement) states that it must be placed on a
> !Tor and she is ravnos???

No. I say that her controller plays the card as if she is a Toreador
antitribu (since the card requires a Toreador antitribu), and so the
play of the card considers her a Toreador antitribu, so it can be
played on her.

Once it is on her, she gets the benefit, since the benefit is not
keyed to "This Toreador antitribu" (something for which she no
longer qualifies), but rather "This vampire" (and she is a vampire).
